topic: Trains - track ballast (crushed stone under the rails)
question: WHY BUILD RAILWAYS
ON CRUSHED STONE?
options: To stop sparks from starting fires
To lock the track in place
To keep animals off the line
answer_full: To lock the track in place. The stones are called track ballast
recap: Most railway lines are built on a thick bed of sharp, crushed rock, and heavy freight trains thunder over it every day.
explain: The sharp, angular stones wedge into each other and grip the concrete ties, so the track can't slide sideways. Smooth, round pebbles would just roll away.
They also spread the huge weight of the train over a wide area of ground.
And rain drains straight through the gaps, so the ground underneath stays firm.
